resources.string: "RedMonitor is a local system-monitoring app. By default, all data stays on your device. Optionally, you can enable anonymized cloud telemetry and an encrypted backup — both can be turned off again at any time in the settings."
"# Privacy Policy — RedMonitor App\n\nLast updated: %1$s"

"## 1. Controller

%1$s
%2$s

"## 2. Scope\n\nThis privacy policy applies to the Android app \"RedMonitor\" and to the backend service at %1$s, insofar as it is contacted by the app."

"## 3. Local data processing (on your device)

The app reads system metrics (CPU, RAM, battery, sensors, network, wake locks, running processes and much more) exclusively locally from Android APIs and — where available — via the Shizuku bridge. This data is stored in RAM and in local SQLite files (Room). It does NOT leave the device unless you explicitly enable the optional cloud sync feature (see section 4).

Stored locally are, among others:
- App settings (SharedPreferences)
- Battery history of the last 30 days (coulomb counter + charge level every 15 minutes)
- Benchmark results (at your request)
- HUD configuration
- Notification log (RAM only, max. 500 entries, no disk persistence)"
"## 4. Optional cloud synchronization\n\nIf you leave the feature enabled in the settings under \"Cloud Backup\" (default: on), the app sends the following data to %1$s at regular intervals:"

"### 4.1 Heartbeat (every ~6 hours)
- Device ID: SHA-256 hash of hardware properties (ANDROID_ID,
 Build.MANUFACTURER, .MODEL, .BOARD, .HARDWARE, .BOOTLOADER) plus a
 salt baked into the app. The ID is opaque — NO identifying data can be
 derived from it.
- App version (e.g. "1.6.2")
- Android version (SDK level + release string)
- Device brand and model (e.g. "Xiaomi", "Mi 11")
- SoC designation (e.g. "taro qcom-sm8450")
- Network type (wifi / mobile / none) — NO Wi-Fi names, NO IP
- Battery charge level in %
- Uptime in seconds

Purpose: aggregate statistics (how many users, which device classes, which
app versions are active). Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest
in product improvement). When cloud sync is disabled, NO heartbeat takes place."

"### 4.2 Encrypted backup (every ~24 hours)
Content: SharedPreferences values, HUD configuration, update preferences,
battery sample history of the last 30 days — serialized as JSON,
**end-to-end encrypted** with AES-256-GCM. The key is derived via
HKDF-SHA256 from your hardware fingerprint and NEVER leaves the device.

The server stores only opaque encrypted bytes and cannot decrypt the
content, not even upon request by authorities. In addition, the blob is held
in the Postgres database with pgcrypto column encryption (defense-in-depth,
at-rest layer).

Purpose: restoring your settings after reinstalling the app or resetting the
device on the same hardware."

"### 4.3 Benchmark comparison (only upon explicit confirmation)

In the benchmark history you can contribute a single result to compare your
device with others. This is **never automatic**: you confirm each individual
upload in a dialog that first lists what will be transmitted. There is no
remembered consent and no "don't ask again".

Transmitted are: benchmark type, total score, single- and multi-core score,
the sub-scores of the run, device model, manufacturer, SoC designation,
Android SDK level and app version — linked to the same anonymous device
identifier as in section 4.1.

Not transmitted are: name, account, location, installed apps or other
usage data.

Retrieving the comparison values is separate from this: for that, only
benchmark type, SoC designation and the score to be compared are sent as a
request to the server, **without** a device identifier, and nothing is stored
in the process. You can therefore also see the comparison values without
contributing anything yourself.

Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR (consent, individually per upload)."

"## 5. Storage period

Data on the backend is deleted automatically:
- Heartbeats: 90 days after receipt
- Backups: 90 days after upload
- Contributed benchmark scores: 90 days after upload
- Device records: 90 days after the last heartbeat
- Admin sessions: after expiry (max. 14 days)

An automatic cleanup job runs every 24 hours on the server."

"## 6. Server location and security

The backend server is located in Germany. Postgres is bound to 127.0.0.1
only, and the HTTP server likewise listens only locally behind an nginx
reverse proxy with HTTPS (Let's Encrypt) + HSTS (max-age 2 years)."

"## 7. Recipients / third-country transfer

NO data transfer to third countries takes place. There are no advertising
trackers, no analytics SDKs, no crash reporters such as Firebase."

"## 8. Your rights (GDPR)

You have the right at any time to:
- Access (Art. 15)
- Rectification (Art. 16)
- Erasure (Art. 17) — see section 9
- Restriction of processing (Art. 18)
- Data portability (Art. 20)
- Objection (Art. 21)
- Complaint to the competent data protection authority

Contact for GDPR requests: %1$s"

"## 9. Deletion of your cloud data

Immediate deletion of your backend record:
1. Open the app → Settings → Cloud Backup → toggle OFF, or
2. Contributed benchmark scores: Info → Privacy Dashboard →
 "Delete uploaded benchmark scores" (takes effect immediately and permanently), or
3. E-mail to %1$s with your device ID (viewable
 in the app settings under "Cloud Backup")

After automatic 90-day inactivity, the data is deleted anyway."

"## 10. App permissions

Depending on the feature used, the app requests permissions (location for the
GPS test, microphone for the mic test, camera for the flash test, etc.). These
permissions are used exclusively locally for the respective test — the
captured sensor/audio/image data does NOT leave the device."

"## 11. Changes to this privacy policy

In the event of material changes, the version number is incremented. You will
be asked for your consent again the next time you start the app."

"## 2. License and open source

The app is provided free of charge. The source code is publicly available on
GitHub (theredstonee/redmonitor) under the MIT license."

"## 3. Personal responsibility

RedMonitor is a technical tool for analyzing and modifying system properties.
You use the app at your own risk. In particular, the following applies:"

"### 3.1 Destructive features
The following features can temporarily stress the device or delete data.
They are clearly marked as such and require separate confirmation:

- **Stress test / battery drainer**: generates maximum CPU/GPU load and can
 heat the device up significantly. Potential battery aging during continuous
 operation.
- **Russian Roulette**: randomly rolls destructive actions (app crash,
 SystemUI crash, fork bomb, shutdown). 5% chance of a fork bomb that makes
 the device sluggish until the next hardware reboot. 2% chance of an
 immediate shutdown without saving running processes.
- **Shizuku operations**: with granted Shizuku rights, the app can change
 system settings (DPI, animation, charging stop), force-stop apps, revoke
 permissions, etc. Incorrect operation can render the system unusable or
 endanger the data of other apps.

The provider is NOT liable for damage caused by the deliberate triggering of
such features."

"### 3.2 Charging control
The smart charging-stop function writes directly into the kernel sysfs. On
incompatible devices, the charging status can get stuck. A reboot usually
solves the problem; the provider is not liable for battery problems caused by
incorrect sysfs paths."
"## 4. Backend / cloud sync"

"### 4.1 Availability
The cloud sync service at %1$s is operated without any availability
guarantee. Maintenance downtime, server migrations or the final
discontinuation of the service can occur at any time. Where possible, you
will be notified in advance in the app."

"### 4.2 Backup restoration
Backups are end-to-end encrypted — the key is derived from your hardware
fingerprint (see privacy policy). In the event of a hardware change, factory
reset or ANDROID_ID change, the backup CANNOT be restored. It is NOT a
general cross-device synchronization system."

"### 4.3 Data limits
Backup size is limited to 2 MB per upload. Per device, a maximum of the 5
most recent backups are kept; older ones are deleted with each upload. All
data is deleted automatically 90 days after the last heartbeat."

"## 5. User obligations

You undertake:
- Not to misuse the app to harm other people's devices
- To use the destructive features (see 3.1) only on your own devices
- Not to use vulnerabilities/bugs for attacks against third parties
- In the case of security-relevant findings, to carry out responsible
 disclosure by e-mail to %1$s"

"## 6. Disclaimer of liability

The provider is liable without limitation only for damage caused intentionally
or through gross negligence, as well as in accordance with the Product
Liability Act. For slight negligence, the provider is liable only in the event
of a breach of essential contractual obligations, and in that case only up to
the amount of the foreseeable damage typically arising.

In particular, no liability is assumed for:
- Data loss due to destructive features (roulette, stress test, etc.)
- Battery damage due to drain mode or charging-control experiments
- System instability due to Shizuku operations or sysfs writes
- Outage or data loss of the cloud backup service"

"## 7. Changes to the terms of use

In the event of material changes, the version number is incremented. You will
be asked for your consent again the next time you start the app."

"## 8. Final provisions

The place of jurisdiction for all disputes is, to the extent legally
permissible, the registered office of the provider (Schliersee, Landgericht
München II). German law applies.

Should any provision of these terms of use be invalid, the validity of the
remaining provisions shall remain unaffected."
